llms.body:
# CryptoKey.im

> CryptoKey.im is a browser-only (client-side) encryption and steganography toolkit shipped as a
> PWA. Plaintext, passwords and keys are processed entirely inside the user's browser and are never
> uploaded; the service stores no user content. A companion USBKey provides offline/online PRO.
> It also publishes **CKX** — an open container format and integration surface that lets a
> third-party app hand encrypted key/config data to CryptoKey.im (and back).

- Site: https://cryptokey.im/
- CKX integration guide (zh/en): https://cryptokey.im/ckx/guide/
- CKX format specification v1 (normative): https://cryptokey.im/ckx/spec/
- CKX format specification v1 — English: https://cryptokey.im/ckx/spec/en/
- CKX format v1 localized overview (zh-TW, ja, ko, hi, vi, tr, pt, id, fr, de, es): https://cryptokey.im/ckx/spec/<lang>/
- Robots / sitemap: https://cryptokey.im/robots.txt · https://cryptokey.im/sitemap.xml

## Ways to integrate CKX

Four composable modes. Encryption always happens in the browser/client; the API never receives
passwords, payloads, carriers or plaintext.

| Mode | Entry point | Needs domain allowlist | Needs SDK |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A · Deeplink | `https://cryptokey.im/ckx?op=encrypt\|decrypt&ckx=1&app=<origin>` | no (`app` is the postMessage allowlist) | no |
| B · iframe embed | `https://cryptokey.im/ckx/embed/` | yes (`frame-ancestors` allowlist, self-service) | no |
| C · SDK | `@cryptokey/ckx` (browser ESM/UMD bundles) | no (signed capabilities via `/v1/ckx/license/verify`) | yes |
| D · Light API | `https://cryptokey.im/v1/ckx/*` | registration endpoint manages the embed allowlist | no |

### Deeplink parameters
`op` (encrypt|decrypt, required), `ckx=1`, `app` (third-party origin, required, also the postMessage
allowlist), `schema`, `schemaVersion`, `label`, `mode` (text|image|file|video, default text),
`locale`, `theme`, `return=opener|none`, `nonce`, `timeout`, `size`.

### iframe embed protocol
`postMessage` v1. Host → embed: `ckx:init`, `ckx:encrypt`, `ckx:decrypt`, `ckx:cancel`.
Embed → host: `ckx:ready`, `ckx:capabilities`, `ckx:result`, `ckx:plaintext`, `ckx:error`.

Server-side capability check is **lazy**: the embed calls `POST /v1/ckx/embed/capabilities` only when the
host declares/uses signed features (`schema` / `schemaVersion` / `strictMatching` / `shard` / `bulk` /
`pro` / `whiteLabel`), or loads the iframe with `?pro=1` (for an accurate pre-init `ckx:ready` snapshot).
A **free-tier** embed (`text|image|file|video`) makes **no server call** — zero Cloudflare usage.

Image mode (`mode=image`): the embed uses an **optional user-supplied** carrier image (or a host-provided
`ckx:encrypt.carrier` PNG) as the LSB base; if none is provided it generates a **demo carrier**. Use an
original PNG and transfer it as-is — lossy re-compression destroys the payload, and LSB stego is detectable.
Plaintext is only returned after the user explicitly clicks "send plaintext back"; passwords are
never posted.

## Machine-readable endpoints (all no-plaintext)

- `GET https://cryptokey.im/v1/ckx/release`
  → `sdkVersion`, `formatVersion`, `minSupportedFormat`, `licenseAlg` (Ed25519),
    `licensePublicKey`, `freeFeatures`, `proFeatures`.
- `GET /v1/ckx/embed/policy[?origin=...]` → per-origin only: `{allowed, sla}` + capability tiers
  (no full allowlist; cacheable 60s).
- `GET /v1/ckx/integrators` → full public registry: allowlisted origins + `sla` badges
  (intentional disclosure; the site `/registry` data source).
- `POST /v1/ckx/embed/capabilities` `{origin}` → `{ok, pro, features, proFeaturesGranted, expiresAt, source}`.
- `POST /v1/ckx/embed/register` `{origin}` → registration challenge; then `{origin, verify:true}`.
- `GET | DELETE /v1/ckx/embed/register?origin=...` → registration status (DELETE needs the admin API key).
- `POST /v1/ckx/license/verify` `{app, token?}` → signed-capability check (Ed25519).
- `POST /v1/ckx/usage` `{app, kind}` → best-effort metering (not billing).
- `GET /v1/ckx/schema/{schemaId}` → published field definitions for a schema.

## Capability tiers

- `freeFeatures` (no signing): `text`, `image`, `file`, `video`.
- `proFeatures` (Ed25519-signed license): `shard`, `strictMatching`, `bulk`, `whiteLabel`, `schema`, `sla`.
- Mediums: **A** ciphertext string, **B/C** PNG LSB, **D** `.ckx` (`SAFE` v3 container),
  **E** video trailer append, **G** `CKXA` (asymmetric X25519, no shared password).
- Container: `SAFE` v3 · AES-256-GCM · PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations).

## Domain allowlisting (2 steps)

1. `POST /v1/ckx/embed/register` with `{"origin":"https://app.example"}` → returns a challenge
   token `ckx-verify-<hex>` and the accepted verification file format.
2. Publish exactly that token at `https://app.example/.well-known/cryptokey-ckx.txt`
   (a single line `ckx-verify-<hex>`, or `cryptokey-ckx-verify=ckx-verify-<hex>`; ≤ 4 KB, no
   redirects), then `POST /v1/ckx/embed/register` with `{"origin":"...","verify":true}`.
   The allowlist takes effect within ~60 s without a redeploy.

Details: https://cryptokey.im/ckx/guide/#whitelist

## SDK

- Package name: `@cryptokey/ckx` (mediums A–E, auto carrier detection, capacity pre-check).
- Medium G (asymmetric, no shared password): `CKXA` v1 over X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-256-GCM — `generateRecipientKeyPair`, `encryptToRecipient`, `decryptAsRecipient`, `readRecipientMeta`, `recipientKeyFingerprint`. WebCrypto X25519 only; unsupported runtime → `CKX_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT_VERSION` (no downgrade). Public key = base64url(raw 32 B), private = base64url(PKCS#8).
- Browser ESM: https://cryptokey.im/ckx/sdk/ckx.esm.js
- Type declarations: https://cryptokey.im/ckx/sdk/ckx.d.ts
- Version + sha384 manifest: https://cryptokey.im/ckx/sdk/MANIFEST.json
- Latest zip: https://cryptokey.im/ckx/sdk/ckx-sdk-latest.zip

## Agent tools (CLI / MCP)

- CLI (single-file, Node >= 20, zero deps): https://cryptokey.im/ckx/tools/ckx.mjs
- MCP stdio server: https://cryptokey.im/ckx/tools/ckx-mcp.mjs
- Integrity (sha384): https://cryptokey.im/ckx/tools/MANIFEST.json
- MCP tools: ckx_encrypt, ckx_decrypt, ckx_read_meta, ckx_estimate, ckx_capabilities, ckx_verify_integrity.
- Zero-knowledge: the password comes from an env var / file / stdin (never argv) and is never logged.

## Solutions

Reference designs for building on the CKX open layer. **free/open layer; CKX is not a
database-encryption product** — these are patterns you implement in your own app.

- Backend at-rest encryption (envelope encryption, 13 locales, en/zh translated so far):
  https://cryptokey.im/ckx/solutions/at-rest/
  (English: https://cryptokey.im/ckx/solutions/at-rest/en/ · locales: /zh-TW/ /ja/ /ko/ /hi/ /vi/
  /tr/ /pt/ /id/ /fr/ /de/ /es/ — same content, hreflang-linked, x-default = root)
- In-site pure front-end demo (localStorage only, no upload): https://cryptokey.im/ckx/solutions/at-rest/demo/
  Language: ?lang=<en|zh|zh-TW|ja|ko|hi|vi|tr|pt|id|fr|de|es> (also localStorage[i18nextLng] and
  navigator.language; untranslated locales fall back to en).
- Downloadable demo (dependency-free Node server, ciphertext-only in-memory DB):
  https://cryptokey.im/ckx/solutions/at-rest/atrest-demo-0.1.0.zip
- Scope: per-user DEK wrapped with CKX `SAFE` v3 (passphrase) or `CKXA` v1 (X25519); records use
  AES-256-GCM with `AAD = user_id:record_id`; login != unlock; no `keyFile` field in the open layer
  ("image as key" is an application-level SHA-256 mix-in).
